founder.name: Mercy Wanjau
founder.title: Founder
founder.bio: Mercy Wanjau is a seasoned commercial lawyer, governance professional, and public sector leader. She currently serves as the Secretary to the Cabinet of the Republic of Kenya. Her expertise spans ICT regulation, policy development, corporate governance, and public administration. She has previously served as the Acting Director-General and Director of Legal Services at the Communications Authority of Kenya, where she played a key role in shaping Kenya's digital and regulatory landscape.

objectives.intro: Rooted in a passion for creative problem-solving, we turn ideas into reality and stand as a beacon of hope for those striving for a better tomorrow.

pillars.name: Technology
pillars.description: The Technology pillar is a critical driver of the Mercy Wanjau Foundation's mission to empower Kenyan communities through inclusive growth and social transformation. Focused on bridging Kenya's digital divide, this pillar aims to unlock equal opportunity by enhancing access to digital tools, skills, and innovation. By embedding technology as a catalyst for enhanced outcomes, the pillar embodies the Foundation's vision to be a beacon of hope that illuminates pathways to empowerment, particularly for marginalized groups including youth and persons with disabilities.

pillars.name: Education
pillars.description: The Education & Leadership pillar is a vital driver of the Mercy Wanjau Foundation's mission to empower Kenyan communities through equitable access to knowledge and transformative leadership. In line with our vision to be a beacon of hope, this pillar focuses on closing educational gaps and cultivating leaders who inspire social change. By fostering inclusion especially among youth, women, and persons with disabilities we strengthen the foundation for sustainable community growth across Kenya.

pillars.name: Economic Empowerment
pillars.description: The Economic Empowerment pillar is rooted in the belief that every Kenyan deserves the opportunity to thrive. Guided by our vision to be a beacon of hope driving inclusive growth, social transformation, and empowerment, we are equipping communities with tools, skills, and networks to build sustainable livelihoods. Our mission centers on empowering women, youth, persons with disabilities, and smallholder farmers through practical, locally anchored economic initiatives that foster dignity, resilience, and growth.

pillars.name: Wellness
pillars.description: The Wellness pillar is central to the Mercy Wanjau Foundation's vision of driving inclusive growth and social transformation in Kenyan communities. Focused on the critical intersection of physical and mental health, neither robust economies nor empowering education can thrive without a healthy populace. Our current focus on mental health is delivered through monthly online engagement in partnership with service providers to equip individuals with the skills to have supportive conversations and encourage appropriate professional help or self-help strategies. Early results show appreciation for the information gained, and we are encouraged to continue with preventative, dignity-affirming support and awareness creation.

pillars.name: Disability Inclusion
pillars.description: The Mercy Wanjau Foundation strives to be a beacon of hope by driving social transformation and inclusive growth across Kenya. Our Persons with Disabilities (PWD) pillar is built on the fundamental belief that disability is not inability and that equal access to opportunities, especially in the burgeoning digital economy, is a fundamental right. We directly address the pervasive challenges of limited access to employment, digital exclusion, and societal stigma. While anchored firmly in Kirinyaga County, our model is designed for scalability. We focus on dismantling the barriers of accessibility and lack of inclusive education by forging strategic partnerships with specialized institutions and community service organizations to provide targeted digital skills, assistive technology, and mentorship.
